chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shaza'an, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Salim Abu al-Fadl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The ablution (wudu) is not broken except by what comes out from your two lower ends, which Allah has favored you with.
ai.seo_question: What breaks the ritual ablution (wudu) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, asserting that wudu remains valid until certainty of exit from the two natural orifices (*al-sabilayn*) is established. It serves as the foundational evidence for the majority view that minor emissions, such as wind or pre-seminal fluid, do not break ablution unless confirmed, distinguishing it from the stricter Hanafi position. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on certainty (*yaqin*) over mere suspicion in ritual purity matters.
